sentences.text: Today, we will talk about Kazakhstan.
Kazakhstan is a big, open, and fascinating country in Central Asia.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Kazakhstan?
Kazakhstan is in Central Asia.
It is next to Russia, China, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan.
It also touches the Caspian Sea.
It is the ninth largest country in the world by land.
What is the capital city of Kazakhstan?
The capital city is Astana, also called Nurselton.
The name changed in the past.
Astana is a modern city with tall buildings, wide roads, and cool winters.
Another big city is Almaty, the former capital.
It is in the south and has mountains, parks, and cafes.
Other cities include Shemkaraganda, Akhtal by the Caspian Sea.
How many people live in Kazakhstan?
About 20 million people live in Kazakhstan.
It is a large country with a small population.
Many people live in cities, but there are also villages and nomadic traditions.
What language do people speak in Kazakhstan?
Kazakhstan has two official languages.
Kazakh, the national language, Russian, widely spoken in cities and schools.
Some people also speak English, especially young people and students.
What is the weather like in Kazakhstan?
Kazakhstan has a continental climate.
This means hot summers and very cold winters.
In summer, it is sunny and dry.
In winter, it can snow a lot, especially in the north.
The weather changes depending on the region.
What does Kazakhstan look like?
Kazakhstan has flatlands called Step, mountains in the south and east, deserts in the west, lakes and rivers, forests in some areas.
It is great for nature lovers and open landscapes.
What animals live in Kazakhstan?
In Kazakhstan, you may see eagles, falcons and wolves, horses, camels and sheep, deer, foxes and bears in the mountains, wild Saiga antelope on the step.
Horses are very important in Kazakh culture and history.
What do people eat in Kazakhstan?
Kazakh food is simple, filling and often includes meat.

People eat lamb, beef and horse meat, rice, bread and noodles, dairy products like yogurt and cheese, popular dishes, besh barmak, meat with flat noodles, the national dish, kuyer dak, fried meat with onion and potato, bar sock, fried bread balls, shashlik, grilled meat on skewers, plov, rice with carrots and meat.
What do people drink in Kazakhstan?
People drink tea, usually black tea with sugar, kumis fermented mares milk, shubat fermented camel milk, coffee, juice and water.
Tea is served many times a day, often with snacks and bread.
What is life like in Kazakhstan?
Life in Kazakhstan is a mix of old and new.
People enjoy spending time with family, going to school and university, walking in parks, horse riding or hiking, listening to music or watching TV.
In the countryside, some people still live in yurts, traditional tents.
What are some holidays and traditions in Kazakhstan?
Naris, March 21st, the spring new year with food and music.
Independence Day, December 16th, Unity Day, May 1st, Victory Day, May 9th, Kerbanite and Orazah 8, Muslim holidays.
During Naris, people wear traditional clothes, cook special dishes and say blessings.
Some fun facts about Kazakhstan.
The Kazakh flag is blue with a yellow sun and eagle.
The Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan launched the first human into space.
Nomadic culture is a big part of history.
Yurts, horse games and folk music are still popular.
The name Kazakh means free man.
Now you know many things about Kazakhstan.
You know where it is, what people eat and what they speak.
You learned about traditions, cities and daily life.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
